lines.text: 3. Cisco Secure Email
lines.spoken: 3. Cisco Secure Email.

lines.text: Role and Platforms
lines.spoken: Role and Platforms.

lines.text: Physical appliance, virtual appliance, or cloud service (Chapter 9).
lines.spoken: Physical appliance, virtual appliance, or cloud service (Chapter 9).

lines.spoken: Acts as the email gateway: controls all email connections, accepts messages, and relays them to the right servers.

lines.text: MX Records
lines.spoken: MX Records.

lines.text: The set of MX records for a domain decides how SMTP routes mail.
lines.spoken: The set of MX records for a domain decides how SMTP routes mail.

lines.text: Example 10-11: h4cker.org has five MX records with preference 5, 10, 20, 30, and 40, all pointing to Google servers (gmr-smtp-in.l.google.com and alt1 to alt4), with a TTL of 3600.
lines.spoken: Example 10-11: h4cker dot org has five MX records with preference 5, 10, 20, 30, and 40, all pointing to Google servers (gmr-smtp-in dot l dot google dot com and alt1 to alt4), with a TTL of 3600.

lines.text: Deployment
lines.spoken: Deployment.

lines.text: One interface to filter mail to and from your servers, or two interfaces: one for the Internet and one for internal servers.
lines.spoken: One interface to filter mail to and from your servers, or two interfaces: one for the Internet and one for internal servers.

lines.text: Acts as an MTA and is the destination of the public MX records. The MX records point to its public IP.
lines.spoken: Acts as an MTA and is the destination of the public MX records. The MX records point to its public IP.

lines.text: Must be reachable from the Internet and be the first hop in the email infrastructure.
lines.spoken: Must be reachable from the Internet and be the first hop in the email infrastructure.

lines.text: Figure 10-12 steps:

lines.text: 1. The sender emails omar@secretcorp.org. The client hands it to the sending email server.
lines.spoken: 1. The sender emails omar@secretcorp dot org. The client hands it to the sending email server.

lines.text: 2. The sending server looks up the secretcorp.org MX record, gets mail.secretcorp.org (the Cisco Secure Email), and queries DNS for its IP.
lines.spoken: 2. The sending server looks up the secretcorp dot org MX record, gets mail dot secretcorp dot org (the Cisco Secure Email), and queries DNS for its IP.

lines.text: 3. The sending server opens an SMTP connection to the Cisco Secure Email.
lines.spoken: 3. The sending server opens an SMTP connection to the Cisco Secure Email.

lines.text: 4. The Cisco Secure Email inspects the mail and sends it to the internal mail server if it meets policy and isn't malicious or spam.
lines.spoken: 4. The Cisco Secure Email inspects the mail and sends it to the internal mail server if it meets policy and isn't malicious or spam.

lines.text: 5. The recipient's client gets the mail from the internal server with IMAP or POP.
lines.spoken: 5. The recipient's client gets the mail from the internal server with eye-map or pop.
